questions.s: Concerning the general plan of the brain (Last's):
o: The diencephalon's main parts are the thalamus and hypothalamus
Its cavity is the third ventricle. (Last's page pg 577)
The hindbrain consists of the pons and medulla only
It consists of the pons, medulla oblongata and cerebellum. (Last's page pg 577)
The medulla becomes the spinal cord where the first cervical nerve roots emerge
Last's. (Last's page pg 577)
CSF leaves the ventricles through foramina in the roof of the third ventricle
Its only exit is through foramina in the roof of the fourth ventricle, in the medulla. (Last's page pg 577)

questions.s: The surfaces of the cerebral hemisphere:
o: The orbital surface of the frontal lobe is slightly concave
From the impression of the anterior cranial fossa. (Last's page pg 577)
The temporal pole is concave in conformity with the middle cranial fossa
The temporal pole is boldly convex. (Last's page pg 577)
The under surface of the occipital lobe slopes downwards and outwards
Conforming with the tentorium. (Last's page pg 577)
The under surface is more regular than the medial surface
The under surface is more irregular than the medial surface. (Last's page pg 577)

questions.s: Regarding the lobes of the cerebral hemisphere:
o: They are named after the cranial bones that lie adjacent
Last's. (Last's page pg 577)
The parietal lobe lies behind the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus
Last's. (Last's page pg 577)
The occipital lobe lies above and behind the parieto-occipital sulcus
It lies below and behind the parieto-occipital sulcus. (Last's page pg 577)
The dominant hemisphere is usually slightly smaller than the other
One hemisphere, usually the left in right-handers, is slightly larger and constitutes the dominant hemisphere. (Last's page pg 577)
The part on the lateral surface is strictly the posterior ramus
Last's. (Last's page pg 577-9)
The anterior and ascending rami penetrate the inferior frontal gyrus
Dividing it into orbital, triangular and opercular parts. (Last's page pg 577-9)
The insula is almost completely surrounded by the cingulate sulcus
By the circular sulcus. (Last's page pg 577-9)
The opercula are formed by frontal, parietal and occipital cortex
Frontal, parietal and temporal cortex. (Last's page pg 577-9)
Indents the superior border just behind the midpoint
Last's. (Last's page pg 577-9)
Is the only long sulcus to pass on to the medial surface
Last's. (Last's page pg 577-9)
Usually runs directly into the lateral sulcus
It does not usually run into the lateral sulcus, a useful identifying point. (Last's page pg 577-9)
Is enclosed on the medial surface by the cuneus
By the paracentral lobule. (Last's page pg 577-9)

questions.s: Regarding the parietal and occipital lobes on the lateral surface:
o: The supramarginal gyrus closes the posterior end of the lateral sulcus
Last's. (Last's page pg 577-9)
The supramarginal gyrus closes the posterior end of the superior temporal sulcus
The angular gyrus closes the superior temporal sulcus. (Last's page pg 577-9)
The preoccipital notch is indented by a fold of dura over the transverse sinus
Last's. (Last's page pg 577-9)
The occipital demarcation line slopes downwards at 90 degrees from the parieto-occipital sulcus
At a 45 degree slope to the preoccipital notch. (Last's page pg 577-9)

questions.s: The medial surface of the hemisphere:
o: The cingulate gyrus lies above the corpus callosum
With the cingulate sulcus above it. (Last's page pg 579-81)
The precuneus lies between the parieto-occipital sulcus and the paracentral lobule
Last's. (Last's page pg 579-81)
The cuneus is limited superiorly by the calcarine sulcus
The cuneus is limited inferiorly by the calcarine sulcus. (Last's page pg 579-81)
The parieto-occipital sulcus is horizontal
It is oblique. (Last's page pg 579-81)

questions.s: The calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci form a Y on its side; regarding this:
o: The common stem is the anterior part of the calcarine sulcus
Last's. (Last's page pg 579-81)
The two limbs are the parieto-occipital sulcus and the posterior part of the calcarine sulcus
Last's. (Last's page pg 579-81)
The lingual gyrus lies above the posterior part of the calcarine sulcus
It lies below; the cuneus is above. (Last's page pg 579-81)
The lingual gyrus is limited inferiorly by the occipitotemporal sulcus
By the collateral sulcus. (Last's page pg 579-81)

questions.s: The inferior surface of the brain:
o: The olfactory bulb lies on the gyrus rectus
Last's. (Last's page pg 581)
The olfactory tract runs in the collateral sulcus
In the olfactory sulcus alongside the gyrus rectus. (Last's page pg 581)
The occipitotemporal sulcus lies lateral to the collateral sulcus
Last's. (Last's page pg 581)
The parahippocampal gyrus lies lateral to the collateral sulcus
It lies medial to the collateral sulcus. (Last's page pg 581)

questions.s: Midline structures on the base of the brain:
o: The tuber cinereum lies behind the optic chiasma
The pituitary stalk projects down from it. (Last's page pg 581)
The mamillary bodies lie in front of the tuber cinereum
They lie behind it. (Last's page pg 581)
The posterior perforated substance lies deep in the angle between the cerebral peduncles
Behind the mamillary bodies. (Last's page pg 581)
The anterior perforated substance lies on the temporal lobe medial to the uncus
It lies on the inferior surface of the frontal lobe immediately lateral to the chiasma. (Last's page pg 581)
The thalamus is the largest mass of cells in each hemisphere
It belongs to the diencephalon. (Last's page pg 581)
The corpus striatum is the caudate nucleus and putamen
Joined by interconnecting fibres. (Last's page pg 581)
The globus pallidus is the outer part of the lentiform nucleus
The putamen is the outer part; the globus pallidus is the inner part. (Last's page pg 581)
The main efferent pathway of the corpus striatum arises from the caudate nucleus
From the globus pallidus. (Last's page pg 581)
The tail of the caudate joins the amygdaloid body
Last's. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The whole length of the caudate convexity projects into the lateral ventricle
Last's. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The putamen is small and conical; the globus pallidus large and quadrilateral
The putamen is large and roughly quadrilateral; the globus pallidus small and bluntly conical. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The putamen joins the caudate head across the posterior limb of the internal capsule
Through the anterior part of the internal capsule, giving the striated appearance. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The amygdala lies in the roof of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle
Connected with the tip of the caudate tail. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The amygdala lies in the floor of the inferior horn
In the roof; the hippocampus is in the floor. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The claustrum lies lateral to the putamen
Its significance is unknown. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The claustrum lies between the putamen and globus pallidus
It lies lateral to the putamen. (Last's page pg 581-2)
The striatum is the input side, receiving mainly from cortex, thalamus and substantia nigra
Last's. (Last's page pg 582)
The globus pallidus is the output side
To the thalamus, subthalamic nucleus, substantia nigra and reticular formation. (Last's page pg 582)
The ansa lenticularis passes dorsal to the subthalamic nucleus
The ansa lenticularis is ventral; the ansa fascicularis is dorsal. (Last's page pg 582)
The ansa lenticularis passes through the fibres of the internal capsule
The ansa fascicularis (and subthalamic fasciculus) pass through the capsule. (Last's page pg 582)

questions.s: Parkinsonism and the cerebral white matter:
o: Parkinsonism shows a decrease of dopamine in the nigrostriatal pathway
With tremor, rigidity and akinesia. (Last's page pg 583)
Association fibres are confined to their own hemisphere
Last's. (Last's page pg 583)
Most commissural fibres are in the anterior commissure
Most are in the corpus callosum. (Last's page pg 583)
Fibres of the corpus callosum run parallel to the corona radiata without crossing it
They intersect it. (Last's page pg 583)
It lies within the concavity of the C-shaped caudate nucleus
Separating it from the lateral ventricle. (Last's page pg 583)
In horizontal section it is bent into a lateral concavity by the globus pallidus
Last's. (Last's page pg 583)
The anterior limb lies between the thalamus and lentiform nucleus
Between the head of the caudate and lentiform nucleus. (Last's page pg 583)
Frontopontine fibres occupy the lateral third of the base of the peduncle
The medial third. (Last's page pg 583)

questions.s: Regarding the components of the internal capsule:
o: The genu lies at the apex of the globus pallidus
Last's. (Last's page pg 583)
The genu carries corticonuclear fibres
To the motor nuclei of cranial nerves. (Last's page pg 583)
Corticospinal fibres occupy the posterior two-thirds of the posterior limb
The anterior two-thirds. (Last's page pg 583)
The anterior limb is thought to carry fibres from the frontal eye field to the abducent nucleus for accommodation
To the oculomotor nucleus, for the accommodation-convergence reflex. (Last's page pg 583)

questions.s: In the posterior limb of the internal capsule (Last's):
o: Corticospinal fibres run arm, hand, trunk, leg and perineum from front to back
Last's. (Last's page pg 583-4)
Corticospinal fibres run leg, trunk, arm in order from front to back
Arm, hand, trunk, leg and perineum from front to back. (Last's page pg 583-4)
In the cerebral peduncle head fibres lie medially and perineal fibres laterally
Last's. (Last's page pg 583-4)
Striate artery haemorrhage here typically causes ipsilateral flaccid paralysis
Contralateral spastic paralysis, an upper motor neuron lesion. (Last's page pg 583-4)

questions.s: Fibre numbers in the internal capsule and corpus callosum:
o: Corticopontine fibres are the largest group in the internal capsule
About 20 million. (Last's page pg 585)
Corticospinal fibres are the largest group in the internal capsule
Corticopontine fibres are the largest group. (Last's page pg 585)
The corpus callosum has about 100 million fibres
Last's. (Last's page pg 585)
The corpus callosum becomes thinner from front to back
It becomes increasingly thicker, ending as the thick splenium. (Last's page pg 585)
Commences at the anterior commissure at the upper end of the lamina terminalis
Last's. (Last's page pg 585)
The rostrum passes upwards and forwards from the anterior commissure
Then turns back as the genu. (Last's page pg 585)
Has three parts: genu, body and splenium
Four parts: rostrum, genu, body and splenium. (Last's page pg 585)
Ends posteriorly as a thin tapering edge
It ends as a thick rounded free border, the splenium. (Last's page pg 585)
Genu fibres form the forceps minor
Arching to the frontal lobe. (Last's page pg 586)
Splenial fibres form the forceps minor
They form the forceps major, to the occipital lobes. (Last's page pg 586)
Fibres form the roof of the anterior horn and body of the lateral ventricle
Last's. (Last's page pg 586)
The tapetum forms the medial wall of the inferior and posterior horns
It forms the lateral wall. (Last's page pg 586)
MsI includes Brodmann areas 4 and 6
The old motor and premotor regions. (Last's page pg 586)
MsII is the supplementary motor area on the medial frontal surface
Parts of areas 6 and 8. (Last's page pg 586)
SmI corresponds to areas 40 and 43
SmI is areas 3, 1 and 2; SmII is areas 40 and 43. (Last's page pg 586)
SmII is the uppermost part of the postcentral gyrus
It is the lowest part. (Last's page pg 586)
MsI receives its main inputs from the cerebellum and thalamus
Last's. (Last's page pg 586)
MsII receives many fibres from the basal nuclei
Concerned with postural mechanisms. (Last's page pg 586)
In the precentral gyrus the face is represented upside down
The body is upside down but the face itself is the right way up. (Last's page pg 586)
The hand area lies below the face area
The face lies lowest, then the hand. (Last's page pg 586)
Broca's area is areas 44 and 45
Last's. (Last's page pg 586)
Broca's area is centred on the pars triangularis
Between the anterior and ascending rami of the lateral fissure. (Last's page pg 586)
Damage to Broca's area paralyses the laryngeal muscles
It causes motor aphasia but not paralysis of laryngeal musculature. (Last's page pg 586)
Wernicke's area lies in the anterior parts of the superior and middle temporal gyri
In the posterior parts, extending into the lower parietal lobe. (Last's page pg 586)
The frontal eye field is in the centre of the middle frontal gyrus
Parts of areas 6, 8 and 9. (Last's page pg 586)
SmI is associated with pain and temperature
SmI is touch, kinaesthetic and vibration; SmII appears associated with pain and temperature. (Last's page pg 586)
The cortex is necessary for localisation of pain
Conscious appreciation may occur at thalamic level. (Last's page pg 586)
The gustatory area is in the superior part of the postcentral gyrus
In the inferior part (frontoparietal operculum), near the tongue area. (Last's page pg 586)
The auditory area is areas 41 and 42
In the anterior transverse temporal gyrus. (Last's page pg 586)
The auditory association area is area 21
Area 22. (Last's page pg 586)
A lesion of one auditory cortex does not cause deafness
The cochleae are bilaterally represented. (Last's page pg 586)
The olfactory area is in the posterior part of the parahippocampal gyrus
In the uncus, at the front of the parahippocampal gyrus. (Last's page pg 586)
It lies along the lower lip of the anterior part of the calcarine sulcus
And both lips of the posterior part. (Last's page pg 586-7)
It lies along the upper lip of the anterior part of the calcarine sulcus
The lower lip of the anterior part. (Last's page pg 586-7)
It extends about 1 cm on to the lateral surface as far as the lunate sulcus
Last's. (Last's page pg 586-7)
The visual association areas are 17 and 18
18 and 19; area 17 is the striate cortex. (Last's page pg 586-7)
The stria of Gennari bisects the grey matter of the striate cortex
Visible to the naked eye. (Last's page pg 586-7)
The upper half of each visual cortex receives from the upper half of each half-retina
So upper and lower visual fields are crossed. (Last's page pg 586-7)
The macula registers at the anterior end of the visual area
At the posterior end. (Last's page pg 586-7)
The temporal half of the retina receives from the temporal half of the visual field
From the nasal half of the field. (Last's page pg 586-7)
The bipolar cells represent the posterior root ganglion cells of other pathways
Last's. (Last's page pg 587)
Ganglion cells are about 1 per cone and 1 per 80 rods
Last's. (Last's page pg 587)
Ganglion cells lie in the outer part of the retina next to the choroid
In the inner part next to the vitreous. (Last's page pg 587)
The optic nerve regenerates effectively after division
It is CNS white matter with no effective regeneration. (Last's page pg 587)
The dura and arachnoid leave the nerve at the optic foramen
It continues sheathed in pia. (Last's page pg 587)
The chiasma is attached to the anterior part of the floor of the third ventricle
Last's. (Last's page pg 587)
The right optic tract carries the temporal field of the right eye
It carries the nasal field of the right eye and the temporal field of the left eye. (Last's page pg 587)
There is a further decussation of visual fibres between the optic tract and the cortex
No further decussation. (Last's page pg 587)

questions.s: The optic tract divides into two branches; regarding these:
o: The larger enters the lateral geniculate body
Visual fibres synapse there. (Last's page pg 587)
The superior brachium is the larger branch
It is the smaller medial branch. (Last's page pg 587)
The superior brachium passes between the lateral and medial geniculate bodies
Last's. (Last's page pg 587)
The superior brachium mediates conscious vision
It mediates light reflexes, to superior colliculus and pretectal nuclei. (Last's page pg 587)
Lies below the pulvinar on the posterior surface of the thalamus
Last's. (Last's page pg 587)
Has six layers
Last's. (Last's page pg 587)
Receives uncrossed fibres in layers 1, 4 and 6
Uncrossed (temporal) fibres go to layers 2, 3 and 5. (Last's page pg 587)
Projects to the visual cortex via the superior brachium
Via the optic radiation (geniculocalcarine tract). (Last's page pg 587)
The superior colliculi are united by the posterior commissure
At the entrance to the aqueduct. (Last's page pg 587-8)
Pupillary light reflex fibres pass bilaterally to the pretectal nuclei
Last's. (Last's page pg 587-8)
Pupillary light reflex fibres synapse in the superior colliculus
They do not; they go to the pretectal nucleus. (Last's page pg 587-8)
An Argyll Robertson pupil contracts to light but not to accommodation
It loses contraction to light but contracts to accommodation and convergence. (Last's page pg 587-8)
Lies in the tegmentum under the upper and lateral margin of the superior colliculus
Last's. (Last's page pg 587-8)
Sends light impulses to each Edinger-Westphal nucleus
Last's. (Last's page pg 587-8)
Is the site of the lesion producing an Argyll Robertson pupil
Last's. (Last's page pg 587-8)
Sends fibres down as the tectospinal tract
That arises from the superior colliculus. (Last's page pg 587-8)

questions.s: Components of the limbic system listed by Last's include:
o: The septal and piriform areas near the lamina terminalis
Last's. (Last's page pg 588-9)
The insula
Along with the uncus, cingulate and parahippocampal gyri. (Last's page pg 588-9)
The mammillary body
With hippocampus, fimbria and fornix. (Last's page pg 588-9)
The claustrum
Not listed; its significance is unknown. (Last's page pg 588-9)
It is an elongated extension of the white matter of the brain
Like the optic nerve. (Last's page pg 588-9)
Its posterior end is expanded as the olfactory bulb
The anterior end. (Last's page pg 588-9)
The second neuron reaches the cortex without thalamic relay
Unique. (Last's page pg 588-9)
Its fibres reach the uncus through the posterior perforated substance
Through the anterior perforated substance. (Last's page pg 588-9)
It is the hippocampal sulcus projected into the floor of the inferior horn
Last's. (Last's page pg 589)
The alveus is a thin film of white matter on its ventricular surface
Its fibres thicken medially to form the fimbria. (Last's page pg 589)
The pes hippocampi is its posterior part
The pes is the anterior part, like the knuckles of a clenched fist. (Last's page pg 589)
The dentate gyrus lies between the fimbria and the cingulate gyrus
Between the fimbria and the parahippocampal gyrus. (Last's page pg 589)
Is the great efferent pathway from the hippocampus
Last's. (Last's page pg 589)
Its commissure is really a chiasma
An association tract rather than a true commissure. (Last's page pg 589)
Its body lies above the corpus callosum
Beneath the corpus callosum. (Last's page pg 589)
Its anterior columns form the posterior margins of the interventricular foramina
They form the anterior margins. (Last's page pg 589)

questions.s: The columns of the fornix and Papez circuit:
o: The columns pass both anterior and posterior to the anterior commissure
Last's. (Last's page pg 589)
The precommissural fibres pass to nuclei within the septum pellucidum
To the septal nuclei near the lamina terminalis, not in the septum pellucidum. (Last's page pg 589)
The mamillothalamic tract runs in the lateral wall of the third ventricle
To the anterior pole of the thalamus. (Last's page pg 589)
The anterior thalamic neurons project to the parahippocampal gyrus
Through the internal capsule to the cingulate gyrus. (Last's page pg 589)
Is a thin film of grey matter on the upper surface of the corpus callosum
Last's. (Last's page pg 589)
Overlies the medial and lateral longitudinal striae
Last's. (Last's page pg 589)
Lies on the under surface of the corpus callosum
On the upper surface. (Last's page pg 589)
Contains striae that are aberrant fibres of the cingulum
Aberrant fibres of the fornix. (Last's page pg 589)
A choroid plexus forms where ependyma contacts pia with no nervous tissue between
Allowing capillaries to invaginate. (Last's page pg 589-90)
The lateral ventricle plexuses secrete the bulk of the CSF
Last's. (Last's page pg 589-90)
The fourth ventricle plexus is continuous with the third ventricle plexus
It is separate and makes only a small contribution. (Last's page pg 589-90)
The third ventricle comes to the surface in its floor
On its roof, invaginated by two choroid plexuses. (Last's page pg 589-90)
The central canal extends into the upper end of the filum terminale
Last's. (Last's page pg 589-90)
The midline ventricles are symmetrical
Last's. (Last's page pg 589-90)
Asymmetry of the lateral ventricles is abnormal
Asymmetry, especially posteriorly, is the rule. (Last's page pg 589-90)
Apertures exist in the roof of the third ventricle
The only apertures are in the roof of the fourth ventricle. (Last's page pg 589-90)
It is a C-shaped slit on the medial surface of the hemisphere
Curving around the thalamus and caudate tail. (Last's page pg 590)
It is the medial wall of the body and inferior horn
Last's. (Last's page pg 590)
It extends into the anterior horn
The plexus does not extend into the anterior horn; the fissure is limited anteriorly by the interventricular foramen. (Last's page pg 590)
It forms the lateral wall of the inferior horn
The tapetum closes the inferior horn laterally. (Last's page pg 590)
The calcarine sulcus
As the calcar avis. (Last's page pg 590)
The collateral sulcus
As the collateral eminence. (Last's page pg 590)
The central sulcus
Not listed: the parahippocampal (hippocampal), calcarine and collateral sulci indent it. (Last's page pg 590)
The cingulate sulcus
Not listed. (Last's page pg 590)

questions.s: The anterior horn and body of the lateral ventricle:
o: The anterior horn is bounded by the forceps minor
Fibres from the genu and rostrum. (Last's page pg 590)
The head of the caudate lies in its floor
Meeting the roof laterally. (Last's page pg 590)
The septum pellucidum separates the floor from the roof laterally
Medially. (Last's page pg 590)
The interventricular foramen lies in front of the anterior column of the fornix
Behind the column, between it and the anterior pole of the thalamus. (Last's page pg 590)

questions.s: The floor of the body of the lateral ventricle:
o: Is formed by the thalamus and body of caudate
With the thalamostriate groove between. (Last's page pg 590)
A band of white matter running the whole length of the caudate lies in the thalamostriate groove
Last's: it runs from the amygdaloid body at the tail to the anterior perforated substance at the head (usually named the stria terminalis). (Last's page pg 590)
The thalamostriate vein runs in the roof
It runs in the groove in the floor. (Last's page pg 590)
The roof is formed by the septum pellucidum alone
The corpus callosum, with the crus and body of fornix medially. (Last's page pg 590)
It is the most variably developed and may be absent
Last's. (Last's page pg 590-1)
The bulb of the posterior horn is formed by the forceps major
Upper convexity on the medial wall. (Last's page pg 590-1)
The calcar avis is the upper convexity on the medial wall
It is the lower convexity, formed by the calcarine sulcus. (Last's page pg 590-1)
The optic radiation lies in the medial wall
It lies against the tapetum in the lateral wall. (Last's page pg 590-1)
It is the largest horn
Last's. (Last's page pg 591-2)
The hippocampus forms the medial part of its floor
With the collateral eminence laterally. (Last's page pg 591-2)
The tail of the caudate lies in its floor
In the roof. (Last's page pg 591-2)
The fimbria forms the upper lip of the choroid fissure here
The fimbria forms the lower lip; the fornix forms the upper lip in the body. (Last's page pg 591-2)

questions.s: The C-shape of the lateral ventricle:
o: Structures around the convexity appear in the roof of the body and floor of the inferior horn
Last's. (Last's page pg 591-2)
The amygdala lies to the lateral side of the anterior perforated substance
Bulging the roof at the tip of the inferior horn. (Last's page pg 591-2)
Structures in the concavity appear in the roof of the body
In the floor of the body and roof of the inferior horn. (Last's page pg 591-2)
The internal capsule lies outside the concavity of the caudate
It lies within the concavity of the caudate. (Last's page pg 591-2)

questions.s: The anterior wall and floor of the third ventricle:
o: The lamina terminalis extends from the rostrum of the corpus callosum to the chiasma
Last's. (Last's page pg 592-3)
The anterior commissure lies in the upper part of the lamina terminalis
Joining the two piriform areas. (Last's page pg 592-3)
The anterior commissure joins the two cingulate gyri
The two piriform areas. (Last's page pg 592-3)
The floor ends at the anterior perforated substance
It extends back to the posterior perforated substance. (Last's page pg 592-3)

questions.s: The septum pellucidum and third ventricle (Last's):
o: The cavum septi pellucidi is lined with pia, not ependyma
Last's. (Last's page pg 593)
The cavum septi pellucidi communicates with the ventricular system
It has no connexion; "fifth ventricle" should be avoided. (Last's page pg 593)
The interthalamic adhesion is not a commissure
No interchange of fibres. (Last's page pg 593)
The interthalamic adhesion is present in about 20% of brains
About 60% (two-thirds). (Last's page pg 593)
The hypothalamus lies below the hypothalamic groove
Including the floor. (Last's page pg 594)
The subthalamic nucleus lies on the medial side of the internal capsule
Adjacent to the substantia nigra. (Last's page pg 594)
The subthalamic nucleus belongs functionally to the limbic system
To the basal nuclei. (Last's page pg 594)
Supraoptic axons control the anterior lobe through the portal vessels
Supraoptic and paraventricular axons run to the posterior lobe. (Last's page pg 594)

questions.s: The roof of the third ventricle (Last's):
o: The medullary striae join posteriorly in the habenular commissure
Last's. (Last's page pg 594-5)
The habenular commissure is probably olfactory
Like the anterior commissure. (Last's page pg 594-5)
The suprapineal recess lies within the pineal stalk
That is the pineal recess; the suprapineal recess lies between pineal and habenular commissure. (Last's page pg 594-5)
The roof is a thick layer of nervous tissue
It is pia lined with ependyma. (Last's page pg 594-5)
Lies above the superior colliculi, below the splenium
Last's. (Last's page pg 595)
Lacks a blood-brain barrier
Last's. (Last's page pg 595)
Is normally calcified on radiographs before age 20
Normally after the age of forty. (Last's page pg 595)
Secretes melatonin with a gonadotrophic action
Antigonadotrophic action. (Last's page pg 595)

questions.s: Regarding the pineal stalk and thalamus:
o: The posterior commissure connects the two superior colliculi
Above the entrance to the aqueduct. (Last's page pg 595)
The pineal recess lies between the habenular and posterior commissures
Last's. (Last's page pg 595)
The neothalamus lies on the medial side of the thalamus
On the lateral side. (Last's page pg 595)
The thalamus is part of the cerebral hemisphere
It is part of the wall of the diencephalon. (Last's page pg 595)
The medial walls of the two thalami lie parallel
Joined in two-thirds of cases. (Last's page pg 595-6)
The pulvinar is the large posterior convexity
The lateral geniculate bulges from its lateral part. (Last's page pg 595-6)
The anterior pole is large and the pulvinar small
Small blunt anterior pole, large pulvinar. (Last's page pg 595-6)
The medial geniculate body relays through the retrolentiform internal capsule
Through the sublentiform part. (Last's page pg 595-6)
The lateral surface is bevelled by the internal capsule
Last's. (Last's page pg 596)
The anterior pole lies at the interventricular foramen
Covered with ependyma. (Last's page pg 596)
The inferior surface is wider than the superior
Narrower. (Last's page pg 596)
The superior surface is entirely covered with ependyma
It is on the external surface, covered with pia; only a lateral strip is ependyma-covered. (Last's page pg 596)
The ventroposterior part of the lateral nuclei receives the medial and spinal lemnisci
Projecting to sensory cortex. (Last's page pg 596)
Parts of the lateral nucleus receive from the dentate nucleus and globus pallidus
Projecting to motor areas. (Last's page pg 596)
The anterior nucleus receives the mamillothalamic tract and projects to the frontal eye field

The neural tube cavity reaches the surface at two places, both dorsal
Forebrain and hindbrain. (Last's page pg 597)

First forwards (rostrum) then backwards. (Last's page pg 597)

Association fibres. (Last's page pg 597)

The internal capsule almost separates caudate from lentiform nucleus

The corpus striatum develops in the roof of the cerebral vesicle
In the floor. (Last's page pg 598-9)

The original dorsal roof plate. (Last's page pg 598-9)
The insula and piriform area are remnants of the archaeopallium
Last's. (Last's page pg 599)
The archaeocerebellum was mainly vestibular

The corpus callosum is the commissure of the archaeopallium
It is the commissure of the neopallium; anterior and posterior commissures unite the archaeopallium. (Last's page pg 599)
The red nucleus appeared with the archaeopallium
It appears with the neopallium, as do the neocerebellum and olivary nucleus. (Last's page pg 599)
The basilar divides at the upper border of the pons
Last's. (Last's page pg 599-600)
The posterior communicating runs through the interpeduncular cistern
Last's. (Last's page pg 599-600)
The anterior communicating lies in the interpeduncular cistern
In the chiasmatic cistern. (Last's page pg 599-600)
The circle encircles the mamillary bodies
Only the optic chiasma and pituitary stalk. (Last's page pg 599-600)
Rupture of circle aneurysms causes about 90% of subarachnoid haemorrhages
Last's. (Last's page pg 599-600)
Aneurysms are commoner on the carotid part of the circle
Last's. (Last's page pg 599-600)

Where the tunica media is weakest, at branching points. (Last's page pg 599-600)
Arteries entering the brain anastomose freely at precapillary level
They are end arteries. (Last's page pg 599-600)
The anterior choroidal does not supply cortex

Surface vessels have sympathetic innervation that is lost intracortically
Last's. (Last's page pg 600)

From the internal carotid termination, or middle cerebral or posterior communicating. (Last's page pg 600)
The perforating branches anastomose with each other
They are invariably end arteries. (Last's page pg 600)

questions.s: Concerning the intracranial internal carotid artery and brain capillaries:

Divides at the anterior perforated substance
Into middle and anterior cerebral. (Last's page pg 600)

On the front half of the roof. (Last's page pg 600)

They lack fenestrations and have abundant tight junctions. (Last's page pg 600)
Is the largest and most direct branch of the internal carotid
Hence most subject to embolism. (Last's page pg 600)
Supplies the insula and overlying opercula
Last's. (Last's page pg 600)
Supplies the superior frontal gyrus
Its territory falls short of the borders by about one gyrus: it does not reach the superior frontal or inferior temporal gyri. (Last's page pg 600)

Passes forwards above the optic nerve

Last's. (Last's page pg 600)
Supplies the inferior temporal gyrus
That is posterior cerebral territory. (Last's page pg 600)
Never arises from the opposite carotid
Occasionally both anterior cerebrals arise from one carotid by a common stem. (Last's page pg 600)

Ophthalmic plus anterior and middle cerebral territories. (Last's page pg 600)

Owing to collateral flow through the arterial circle. (Last's page pg 600)

Contralateral hemiplegia. (Last's page pg 600)
Micturition and defecation areas lie in middle cerebral territory
In anterior cerebral territory. (Last's page pg 600)
Supplies the cerebral peduncle and optic tract as it curls round the peduncle
Last's. (Last's page pg 601)

And a strip of lateral occipital cortex. (Last's page pg 601)
Has the macular visual cortex always wholly within its territory
Middle cerebral branches sometimes supply the macular area, giving macular sparing. (Last's page pg 601)
Arising from the internal carotid is an acquired anomaly
It is persistence of the primitive embryonic pattern. (Last's page pg 601)
They enter through the anterior perforated substance from anterior and middle cerebrals

Medial striate branches supply the genu and posterior limb of the internal capsule

From the anterior cerebral. (Last's page pg 601)

In about 3%. (Last's page pg 601)

Last's. (Last's page pg 601)

From the middle cerebral. (Last's page pg 601)

Posterior cerebral branches enter the posterior perforated substance. (Last's page pg 601)

Contralateral hemiplegia. (Last's page pg 601)
Passes below the optic tract

Enters the choroid fissure at the tip of the inferior horn, just above the uncus
Last's. (Last's page pg 601)
Supplies the anterior limb of the internal capsule
It supplies the posterior part of the internal capsule. (Last's page pg 601)
Supplies the medial geniculate body
It supplies the chiasma, optic tract and lateral geniculate body. (Last's page pg 601)

questions.s: Effects of complete occlusion described by Last's:
o: Anterior cerebral distal to Heubner's artery affects only the opposite leg
Last's. (Last's page pg 601)
Middle cerebral occlusion may cause hemianopia from oedema compressing the optic radiation
Last's. (Last's page pg 601)
Posterior cerebral occlusion causes contralateral hemiplegia
Contralateral hemianopia and hemianaesthesia, and cerebral oedema. (Last's page pg 601)
Anterior choroidal occlusion spares vision
Contralateral hemiplegia, hemianaesthesia and hemianopia. (Last's page pg 601)
Cortical veins travel superficially in the arachnoid
Unlike arteries, deep in the sulci. (Last's page pg 602)
They enter sinuses obliquely against the bloodstream
Last's. (Last's page pg 602)
Superior cerebral veins meeting a blood lake pass between the dural layers
They pass on its cerebral surface beneath the arachnoid. (Last's page pg 602)

Into the cavernous sinus. (Last's page pg 602)
The depths of the lateral sulcus and insula drain by the deep middle cerebral vein
Which joins the basal vein. (Last's page pg 602)

Last's. (Last's page pg 602)

Into the superior sagittal sinus; the inferior anastomotic vein into the transverse. (Last's page pg 602)

Passes round the peduncle below the optic tract
With the fourth nerve and posterior cerebral artery. (Last's page pg 603)

Only the lower parts; the upper parts drain to the internal cerebral vein. (Last's page pg 603)
Joins the straight sinus directly
It joins the great cerebral vein below the splenium. (Last's page pg 603)
Is formed at the interventricular foramen
By choroidal and thalamostriate veins. (Last's page pg 603)
Runs back in the tela choroidea
Last's. (Last's page pg 603)

Septal veins usually join the thalamostriate vein. (Last's page pg 603)
Joins its fellow above the splenium
Beneath the splenium, forming the great cerebral vein. (Last's page pg 603)

questions.s: The structure of the cerebral cortex (Last's):

Abundant fibres, few cells. (Last's page pg 603)
Layer IV is the ganglionic layer
IV is internal granular; V is ganglionic. (Last's page pg 603)
The stria of Gennari is the external band of Baillarger
In the visual cortex. (Last's page pg 603)
Betz cells give rise to about 20% of corticospinal fibres
No more than 2%. (Last's page pg 603)
Sensory cortex has predominantly granular cells
Postcentral, superior temporal, calcarine. (Last's page pg 603)
Betz cells are in layer V of the precentral gyrus
Last's. (Last's page pg 603)
CNS myelin is formed by Schwann cells
By oligodendrocytes. (Last's page pg 603)
Layer II is the external pyramidal layer
Layer II is external granular; III is pyramidal. (Last's page pg 603)
It extends from just above the tentorial aperture to C1
Last's. (Last's page pg 603-5)
The reticular formation continues into the spinal cord
Last's. (Last's page pg 603-5)
The vital centres are anatomically demonstrable nuclei
They are not anatomically demonstrable as distinct nuclei. (Last's page pg 603-5)
Five sections are the minimum needed to understand it
A minimum of seven. (Last's page pg 603-5)
III and IV nuclei are in the midbrain
Last's. (Last's page pg 603-5)
The trigeminal motor nucleus, VI and VII are in the pons
Last's. (Last's page pg 603-5)
The eighth nerve nuclei lie wholly in the medulla
They overlap the pontomedullary junction. (Last's page pg 603-5)
The trigeminal sensory nuclei are confined to pons and medulla
They extend through midbrain, pons and medulla. (Last's page pg 603-5)
Most of it lies in the posterior cranial fossa
Extending from just above the dorsum sellae to the petrous apices. (Last's page pg 606)
The tectum is the part dorsal to the aqueduct
Last's. (Last's page pg 606)
The medial geniculate body lies medial to the superior colliculus
It lies lateral to each superior colliculus. (Last's page pg 606)

Below the inferior colliculi. (Last's page pg 606)

questions.s: The trochlear nerve is unique in that it:

Last's. (Last's page pg 606)
Is the only one emerging dorsally
Last's. (Last's page pg 606)
Is the only one to decussate within the brainstem
Last's. (Last's page pg 606)

The trochlear nerve passes lateral to the oculomotor between the arteries

The basal vein lies ventral to the optic tract
Last's. (Last's page pg 606)

The trochlear nerve enters the cavernous sinus above the free edge of the tentorium
It runs just below the free edge. (Last's page pg 606)

Last's. (Last's page pg 606-7)

To the basal nuclei. (Last's page pg 606-7)

Last's. (Last's page pg 606-7)

Caudal to the oculomotor. (Last's page pg 607)

Last's. (Last's page pg 607)

At the level of the inferior colliculi. (Last's page pg 607)

Lateral to the olive. (Last's page pg 609-10)

Taste via the internal laryngeal nerve

Except stylopharyngeus by the glossopharyngeal. (Last's page pg 610-11)
The spinal trigeminal nucleus lies lateral to the tractus solitarius nucleus
Last's. (Last's page pg 610-11)
Olivocerebellar fibres decussate to enter the inferior cerebellar peduncle
Last's. (Last's page pg 610-11)

Upper limb, via cuneocerebellar fibres. (Last's page pg 610-11)

Ipsilateral vocal fold paralysis from nucleus ambiguus involvement
Last's. (Last's page pg 611-12)

Uncrossed spinal trigeminal tract. (Last's page pg 611-12)
Loss of pain and temperature on the same side of the body
On the opposite side, from the crossed spinal lemniscus. (Last's page pg 611-12)

At inferior colliculus level. (Last's page pg 612)
Lies immediately ventral to the periaqueductal grey

Last's. (Last's page pg 616)
Absent gag reflex tests pontine connexions
It tests vagal connexions in the medulla. (Last's page pg 616)
The apnoea test requires PaCO2 above 30 mm Hg
Above 50 mm Hg (6.7 kPa). (Last's page pg 616)
The superior peduncle enters the midbrain
Last's. (Last's page pg 616)
The archaeocerebellum is concerned with balance
Vestibular mechanisms. (Last's page pg 616)
The palaeocerebellum is associated with the cerebral hemispheres
With spinal mechanisms (limb movements); the neocerebellum with the cerebrum. (Last's page pg 616)
The highest part of the cerebellum lies at the attached margin of the tentorium
At the tentorial notch. (Last's page pg 616)
The horizontal fissure is the deepest sulcus
But of no functional significance. (Last's page pg 617)
The primary fissure separates palaeocerebellum from neocerebellum
Last's. (Last's page pg 617)
The anterior lobe is large and the posterior lobe small
Small anterior lobe, large posterior lobe. (Last's page pg 617)
The primary fissure lies on the inferior surface
On the superior surface, in front of the horizontal fissure. (Last's page pg 617)
The inferior vermis consists of pyramid, uvula and nodule
Last's. (Last's page pg 617)
The nodule lies highest, on the roof of the fourth ventricle
Last's. (Last's page pg 617)
The flocculonodular lobe and pyramid form the archaeocerebellum
The flocculonodular lobe and the lingula. (Last's page pg 617)
The paraflocculus lies above the flocculus
It lies beneath the flocculus, attached mainly to the pyramid. (Last's page pg 617)
Archaeocerebellar lesions cause trunk ataxia
Without nystagmus or tremor. (Last's page pg 617-18)
Neocerebellar lesions cause intention tremor
And hypotonia, pendular jerks, dysdiadochokinesia and nystagmus. (Last's page pg 617-18)
Palaeocerebellar lesions cause reduced muscle reflexes
Increased muscle reflexes with disturbed postural mechanisms. (Last's page pg 617-18)
Cerebellar lesions cause paralysis
They do not cause paralysis. (Last's page pg 617-18)
The dentate opens towards the superior peduncle
Last's. (Last's page pg 618)
From lateral to medial: emboliform, globose, fastigial
EGF. (Last's page pg 618)
The fastigial nucleus belongs to the palaeocerebellum
To the archaeocerebellum. (Last's page pg 618)
Dentate efferents go to the ipsilateral red nucleus
To the contralateral red nucleus and thalamus. (Last's page pg 618)
The molecular layer is superficial
Mostly fibres with few cells. (Last's page pg 618)
Purkinje cells lie between molecular and granular layers
Last's. (Last's page pg 618)
Climbing fibres act through granule cells
Climbing fibres activate Purkinje cells directly; mossy fibres act through granule and basket cells. (Last's page pg 618)
Purkinje dendrites lie parallel to the long axis of a folium
At right angles to it. (Last's page pg 618)
A climbing fibre activates one Purkinje cell
Last's. (Last's page pg 618-19)
A basket cell axon arborises around some 500 Purkinje cells
Last's. (Last's page pg 618-19)
Mossy fibres are terminals of pontine and vestibular fibres
Those are climbing fibres; mossy fibres are spino- and olivocerebellar terminals. (Last's page pg 618-19)
Efferent fibres generally arise from the cortex
From subcortical nuclei. (Last's page pg 618-19)
The superior peduncle is predominantly efferent
Last's. (Last's page pg 619)
The middle peduncle carries fibres from contralateral pontine nuclei
Last's. (Last's page pg 619)
The anterior spinocerebellar tract runs in the inferior peduncle
In the superior peduncle. (Last's page pg 619)
Olivocerebellar fibres come from the ipsilateral olive
From the opposite olive. (Last's page pg 619)
PICA is the largest branch of the vertebral artery
Last's. (Last's page pg 619)
PICA passes between the rootlets of IX and X
After passing below the hypoglossal rootlets. (Last's page pg 619)
AICA arises from the basilar at the upper part of the pons
At the lower part of the pons. (Last's page pg 619)
The superior cerebellar artery winds round the peduncle above the fourth nerve
Below the fourth nerve. (Last's page pg 619)
Superior and posterior surfaces drain to straight and transverse sinuses
Last's. (Last's page pg 619)
The superior vermis drains to the great cerebral vein
At its entrance to the straight sinus. (Last's page pg 619)
The inferior surfaces drain to the superior petrosal sinus
To the inferior petrosal, sigmoid and occipital sinuses. (Last's page pg 619)
Two arteries supply the small upper surface of each hemisphere
One supplies the upper surface; two supply the large under surface. (Last's page pg 619)
In the fetus it reaches S2 vertebra
Last's. (Last's page pg 619-20)
At birth the conus lies opposite L3
Last's. (Last's page pg 619-20)
It reaches its adult level at about 5 years
About 20 years. (Last's page pg 619-20)
The cervical enlargement occupies segments C3 to T1
C5 to T1; vertebral levels C3 to T1. (Last's page pg 619-20)
The lumbosacral enlargement spans segments L2 to S3
Last's. (Last's page pg 619-20)
It lies opposite vertebrae T9 to L1
Last's. (Last's page pg 619-20)
Each anterior root has ten or more rootlets
Three or four. (Last's page pg 619-20)
The roots unite inside the dural theca
They unite in the intervertebral foramina after evaginating the dura separately. (Last's page pg 619-20)
Cervical posterior root ganglia lie just lateral to the foramina
In contact with the vertebral artery. (Last's page pg 620)
The cauda equina consists of nerve roots, not nerves
Last's. (Last's page pg 620)
The filum terminale is part of the cauda equina
It is pia and not classified as part of the cauda. (Last's page pg 620)
Upper thoracic roots kink downwards to reach their foramina
They kink upwards. (Last's page pg 620)
The central canal extends into the upper few mm of the filum
Last's. (Last's page pg 620)
The white commissure lies anterior to the grey commissure
Last's. (Last's page pg 620)
Posterior white columns are largest in the lumbar region
In the cervical region. (Last's page pg 620)
The anterior horn reaches the surface of the cord
It falls short; the posterior horn reaches the surface. (Last's page pg 620)
Medial cells supply trunk muscles
Last's. (Last's page pg 621-2)
Lateral cells supply limbs
Last's. (Last's page pg 621-2)
Dorsal cells of the lateral group supply proximal limb muscles
Ventral cells supply proximal; dorsal cells distal. (Last's page pg 621-2)
The sympathetic lateral horn spans T1 to L4
T1 to L2. (Last's page pg 621-2)
Lamina II is the gelatinous substance
Last's. (Last's page pg 621-2)
The thoracic nucleus is in the medial part of lamina VII
Last's. (Last's page pg 621-2)
Laminae VII and VIII form the nucleus proprius
Laminae III to VI. (Last's page pg 621-2)
Lamina V contains the alpha motor neurons
Lamina IX; lamina V is a main source of anterolateral tract fibres. (Last's page pg 621-2)
Anterior roots divide lateral from anterior white columns
Last's. (Last's page pg 622-3)
Propriospinal fibres lie adjacent to the grey matter
Last's. (Last's page pg 622-3)
Tracts have sharp boundaries throughout the cord
Except in the posterior columns, there are no sharp boundaries. (Last's page pg 622-3)
The posterior column contains descending fibres
It is wholly occupied by ascending gracile and cuneate fibres. (Last's page pg 622-3)
Fibres from the lowest segments lie nearest the midline
Last's. (Last's page pg 622-3)
They carry the sense of bladder and rectal fullness
Last's. (Last's page pg 622-3)
Fibres enter on the lateral side of the posterior roots
On the medial side. (Last's page pg 622-3)
The gracile tract carries upper limb fibres
Lower trunk, lower limb and perineum; the cuneate carries upper limb. (Last's page pg 622-3)
Romberg's sign indicates sensory ataxia
Last's. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Two points 3 mm apart are normally distinguishable on the finger pads
Last's. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Vibration is tested with a 512 Hz fork
Last's: 128 Hz. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Cerebellar ataxia worsens markedly with eyes closed
With cerebellar or labyrinthine ataxia there is little difference. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Lies in front of the lateral corticospinal tract
And in front of the denticulate ligament. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Arises mainly from laminae I and V
Last's. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Fibres cross behind the central canal
In front of the central canal. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Cervical fibres lie most laterally
Sacral fibres lie most laterally; cervical most deeply. (Last's page pg 623-4)
C fibres carry slow pain
Unmyelinated. (Last's page pg 623-4)
A-delta fibres carry fast pain and temperature
Thinly myelinated. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Lissauer's tract fibres run 5-6 segments before synapsing
One or two segments. (Last's page pg 623-4)
Crude touch fibres occupy the lateral part of the tract
The more medial part, and cross less obliquely. (Last's page pg 623-4)
About 10% of anterolateral fibres pass directly to the thalamus
Last's. (Last's page pg 624)
The rest synapse in the reticular formation
Spinoreticulothalamic. (Last's page pg 624)
Endogenous opioid peptides readily cross the blood-brain barrier
They do not. (Last's page pg 624)
Deep pain is tested by pinprick
Pinprick tests superficial pain; squeezing tests deep pain. (Last's page pg 624)
The knife enters in front of the denticulate ligament
To spare the corticospinal tract. (Last's page pg 625)
The cut is made several segments above the desired level
Because fibres cross obliquely. (Last's page pg 625)
Pain relief is usually permanent
It rarely lasts more than a few months (2 years at most). (Last's page pg 625)
It divides the medial part of the anterolateral tract
The lateral part. (Last's page pg 625)
Clarke's column spans all thoracic and first two lumbar segments
Last's. (Last's page pg 625)
The posterior spinocerebellar tract is uncrossed
To the inferior peduncle. (Last's page pg 625)
The anterior spinocerebellar tract is mostly uncrossed
It mostly crosses. (Last's page pg 625)
Cervical proprioception travels in the posterior spinocerebellar tract
Via the accessory cuneate nucleus and cuneocerebellar tract. (Last's page pg 625)
Lies behind the attachment of the denticulate ligament
Last's. (Last's page pg 625)
Arm fibres cross slightly higher than leg fibres
Last's. (Last's page pg 625)
About 25% of fibres supply the upper limb
About 55% end at cervical and T1 levels; 25% for the lower limb. (Last's page pg 625)
Most fibres synapse directly on motor neurons
98% synapse with interneurons in laminae VII and VIII. (Last's page pg 625)
The lateral reticulospinal tract is facilitatory
Last's. (Last's page pg 625)
The medial reticulospinal tract is inhibitory
Last's. (Last's page pg 625)
The anterior corticospinal tract reaches the sacral cord
No lower than the upper thoracic cord. (Last's page pg 625)
The vestibulospinal tract mainly affects distal limb muscles
Trunk and limb girdle muscles. (Last's page pg 625)
A pure pyramidal lesion causes flaccid paralysis
Last's. (Last's page pg 625-6)
Spasticity reflects concomitant extrapyramidal involvement
Last's. (Last's page pg 625-6)
A pure pyramidal lesion can arise in the internal capsule
It is possible from a lesion confined to the medullary pyramid. (Last's page pg 625-6)
Parasagittal meningioma affects both arm areas
It presses on the leg areas of both hemispheres. (Last's page pg 625-6)
The anterior spinal artery forms from both vertebral arteries
At the foramen magnum. (Last's page pg 626)
It supplies the cord anterior to the posterior grey columns
Last's. (Last's page pg 626)
The posterior spinal arteries arise from the anterior spinal artery
From PICA or the vertebral artery. (Last's page pg 626)
The anterior spinal artery is largest in the thoracic region
It may become so small there that it is considered absent. (Last's page pg 626)
Embryonically every segment has a radicular vessel on both sides
Last's. (Last's page pg 626)
Adamkiewicz is slightly commoner on the left
Last's. (Last's page pg 626)
Adamkiewicz always accompanies T10 or T11
It may be anywhere from T7 to L4. (Last's page pg 626)
Lateral sacral arteries never give radicular branches
They are among the parent vessels. (Last's page pg 626)
Pial arteries supply the periphery of the cord
Last's. (Last's page pg 626)
Sacral sparing results from pial supply to superficial sacral fibres
Last's. (Last's page pg 626)
Posterior spinal veins are single
Double, straddling the posterior roots. (Last's page pg 626)
Spinal veins drain to the azygos system in the lumbar region
To lumbar veins; azygos in the thorax. (Last's page pg 626)
Transection above T10 abolishes effective cough
From abdominal and lower intercostal paralysis. (Last's page pg 627)
Perianal sensation tests conduction through the cord
Last's. (Last's page pg 627)
Brown-Sequard causes ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature
Contralateral. (Last's page pg 627)
In anterior spinal artery syndrome touch is lost
The posterior columns and touch remain intact. (Last's page pg 627)
Commonly follows sudden hyperextension of the cervical spine
Last's. (Last's page pg 627)
Causes flaccid upper limb paralysis
Anterior horn damage. (Last's page pg 627)
Lower limb spasticity arises from sacral corticospinal fibres
From lumbar fibres; sacral fibres are more superficial. (Last's page pg 627)
It spares upper limb pain sensation
Deep cervical anterolateral fibres are interrupted. (Last's page pg 627)

questions.s: The sulcus limitans and nuclear columns (Last's):
o: The alar lamina is dorsal and sensory
Last's. (Last's page pg 627)
Autonomic cells lie near the sulcus limitans
Last's. (Last's page pg 627)
Somatic cells lie nearest the sulcus limitans
They lie further away. (Last's page pg 627)
In the fourth ventricle efferent cells lie lateral
They lie medial; afferent cells lateral. (Last's page pg 627)
Somatic motor nuclei lie near the midline
III, IV, VI and XII. (Last's page pg 627-8)
The branchial column is sometimes called special visceral
Last's. (Last's page pg 627-8)
The nucleus ambiguus has migrated medially
It has migrated laterally. (Last's page pg 627-8)
The Edinger-Westphal nucleus has migrated laterally
It migrated medially, cranial to the somatic oculomotor nucleus. (Last's page pg 627-8)
From medial to lateral: visceral, branchial, somatic
The reverse of the motor columns. (Last's page pg 628-9)
Cochlear and vestibular nuclei form a special somatic group lying farthest laterally
Last's. (Last's page pg 628-9)
Each afferent column consists of several separate nuclei
Each is a single nuclear mass. (Last's page pg 628-9)
The dorsal nucleus of the vagus is currently regarded as mixed motor and sensory
Recent authorities regard it as purely motor. (Last's page pg 628-9)

questions.s: The posterior parts of the internal capsule (Last's):
o: Thalamocortical fibres lie beside and behind corticospinal fibres
Last's. (Last's page pg 584-5)
The retrolentiform part carries the optic radiation
From the lateral geniculate body. (Last's page pg 584-5)
The sublentiform part carries the optic radiation
It carries the auditory radiation. (Last's page pg 584-5)
Parieto-, occipito- and temporopontine fibres occupy the medial third of the peduncle base
The lateral third. (Last's page pg 584-5)

questions.s: The floor of the third ventricle (Last's):
o: The median eminence lies at the base of the infundibulum
Part of the tuber cinereum. (Last's page pg 594)
The supraoptic recess lies between lamina terminalis and chiasma
Last's. (Last's page pg 594)
The mamillary bodies indent the inside of the ventricle
They make no mark inside. (Last's page pg 594)
The anterior commissure is a commissure of the neopallium
Of the archaeopallium. (Last's page pg 594)
